newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains on dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains on dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed higher against the dollar and the currency basket on Thursday following the U.S. currency's decline against the mark and yen in Europe, dealers said.
"The shekel rose today following the weakening of the dollar abroad. The dollar's decline pushed the basket down towards the lower edge of the trading band," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
"Despite the basket's decline the central bank was not seen in the market as the basket was only touching the lower edge," he said.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for two months.
"Volume was moderate today ahead of the long Easter weekend," the dealer said.
The Bank of Israel will set its next representative rate on Tuesday.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3610 shekels against 3.3700 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6587 shekels against 3.6592 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7205 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.7131 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 2.0007 shekels after 1.9931 on Wednesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3600 shekels.
